title: Hail Marks on a Texas Shingle Roof
description: A dark circle in the granules is not always a hail hit. Here is how a bruise, a scuff, and foot traffic look different on a Texas shingle.
html:
After a spring storm, the yard is full of leaves and the neighbor already has a contractor in the driveway. The question on your roof is simpler than the pitch you are about to hear: did the hail fracture the shingle, or did it only scuff the surface?

A shingle is a mat, asphalt, and a layer of granules. The granules take the sun. The mat is what keeps water out. Hail that only knocks granules loose is ugly. Hail that bruises the mat is a leak waiting on the next rain.

What a real hail bruise looks like

Stand in the yard with the sun at your back, or look from a ladder only if you are comfortable on one. A hail hit is usually a dark, roughly round spot where the granules are gone and the asphalt looks polished. Press it with a thumb, gently. A bruise often feels softer than the shingle around it. The pattern is scattered, heavier on the slopes that faced the storm, and it shows up on soft metal in the same pass: box vents, flue caps, and the fins on the air conditioner.

Foot traffic looks different. Those marks run in lines, often from the ladder to a vent, and they smear instead of denting. Blistering from heat is a bubble, not a crater. Manufacturing spots tend to repeat in a grid. If the metals on the roof are clean and the only “hits” are in a path, be slow to call it hail.

Cosmetic scuff and a broken mat

Insurers split this for a reason. A scuff that did not crack the mat may still shed water. A hit that fractured the mat will take on water, then the deck, then the ceiling. On a Texas roof that already cooks all summer, a bruised mat does not heal. Heat opens it.

Do not let anyone “prove” damage by scraping granules off with a coin. That creates the mark they just found. Photos of the slope, the gutters, the window screens, and the AC fins are the record. If you want a second set of eyes before you open a claim, request a free inspection or call (281) 541-0027.

What to do with the photos

The Houston homeowner storm checklist is the short list we give Houston homeowners: what to shoot, what to leave alone, and when a tarp is actually needed. If the bruises are widespread, the next conversation is an insurance claim, not a tube of sealant. A few broken tabs on an otherwise solid roof can be a roof repair. A slope full of soft spots is a roof replacement.
